input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM.
input.rationale: § 16.2 imposes a blanket bar on IBM assigning or transferring any rights or duties without MSL's prior written approval, with no affiliate or successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on MSL's approval; the only softened consent standard runs to MSL's own Related Company assignments. That is our walk-away scenario (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out) and it fails every fallback element except the bare consent requirement. § 16.5 (Sale or Merger) only obliges MSL to notify IBM and to procure successor assumption, so it does not give IBM any successor assignment right. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists against IBM anywhere in the Agreement, so that limb is not in issue; the MSL-only assignment bars in the Loan Agreement (p1578) and the confidentiality terms (p1494) benefit us and are left untouched. We have taken the fallback: a mutual successor assignment right on written notice, with consent for other assignments not to be unreasonably withheld, preserving MSL's Related Company consent mechanic.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice and a reasonableness standard on consent in § 16.2.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 16.2 bars IBM from assigning at all without MSL's approval, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, which is our walk-away position. We have moved to our fallback: either Party may assign to a successor on written notice, and consent for any other assignment may not be unreasonably withheld. MSL's Related Company consent right is preserved, and the redundant MSL-only sentence is absorbed into the mutual sentence.

ops.newText: Either Party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the other Party. Otherwise, neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
